item.title: Markpdf: a best in class Markdown -> PDF tool
item.author: ralsina
item.content:encoded: It parses markdown using then takes the HTML and uses libhtml to do layout and finally libharu to create a PDF.Can create a 600 A4 page PDF of Brothers Karamazov in under 5 seconds.Fenced code blocks with syntax highlightingFully justified with hyphenation (includes implementation of the TeX hyphenation algorithm)Outline based on headingsMultiple image types, including svg (requires external tool)Page breaking with widow heading preventionPageless mode: all your PDF is a single page. Yes, you can do a page with all of Brothers Karamazov in it.CSS stylesheets (a few included, user can add customized)There isn’t AFAIK, a tool with this much feature coverage that doesn’t involve installing chrome or TeX or Typst. item.title: Announcing the Fedora Crystal SIG & Matrix Room (Fedora 46+ Readiness)
item.author: renich
item.content:encoded: As part of the initiative to bring Crystal into Fedora Linux as an official, first-class language runtime (Fedora 46 System-Wide Change Proposal), we have established the official Fedora Crystal SIG (Special Interest Group).Our goal is to build a well-maintained, secure, and unbundled Crystal ecosystem for Fedora, EPEL (RHEL/CentOS Stream), and downstream distributions.Whether you are a shard author, a systems engineer, or a Crystal user on Linux, you are warmly invited to join the conversation and help shape how Crystal is packaged and distributed:Shard Compatibility & Packaging: Help test our generator against your favorite shards to ensure clean, offline builds.: Share thoughts on shard versioning, build macros, or distribution needs in our Matrix room.Packaging Co-maintainership: If you’re a Fedora packager (or want to become one), we’d love to have you co-maintain core ecosystem packages like , , , , and web frameworks.Drop by and say hi!

item.title: Different flavours of `Enum`
item.author: straight-shoota
item.content:encoded: There are a number of discussions about potential enhancements to the type.The primary argument against reopening is to have a fixed, final state of all enum members, so there can be no surprises when switching over them (e.g. in exhaustive ).A flaw in that argument is that it equates enum members with values. A member is just giving a name to a value. For example, member is a name for the value returned by .For many (most?) enum types, the set of members contains all legal values. There exists no value that’s not described by a member. But some enum types can have more values than named members. This is typically the case when an enum is not an original concept and reads values from an external source. For example error or status codes such as or . These types have a large domain of possible values, but only a fraction of them is represented as a named member. The rest might not be standardized, is typically irrelevant or platform specific. But that doesn’t mean such unnamed values can ever be observed.Enum types typically allow instantiating arbitrary values through their numeric constructor. So, if that is allowed, we can always be surprised by an unexpected enum value. handles that by raising a runtime error. Adding an additional member on the other hand would result in a compile-time error. error mode! We shouldn’t refuse that with an argument that it may break things, when the alternative might break as well but in a less obvious way.However, it’s pretty uncommon to have an enum type with open values (e.g. which might be instantiated from numerical input) used in exhaustive case.I’ve come to think that we can describe two different flavours of enums:a fixed list of values, all expressed as members.an open list of values, with some common ones as members.(on top of that, there is also the flavour for flag enums)Perhaps we could improve the enum features in the language to separate these use cases more clearly.For example, an enum with a fixed set of values should reject instances with any other value making it impossible to get an unnamed value. It should not be allowed to reopen and add additional members. An enum with open values does not need to be usable in exhaustive case. Reopening and adding additional members is fine.

item.title: How to make your crystal program compile reeeeeally slow
item.author: ralsina
item.content:encoded:
Here is a pretty innocent program that takes a really long time to compile if you use :# big.cr — a def that returns a ~163KB struct by value struct Big getter a : StaticArray(UInt64, 20410) # 20410 * 8 = ~163KB
def initialize @a = StaticArray(UInt64, 20410).new(0_u64) end end
def make : Big big = Big.new big.a[0] = 1_u64 big # returned by value end
x = make y = make puts x.a[0] + y.a[0] Depending on the size of the struct it returns, the compile time shoots to pretty much infinite, and may even use all your RAM.More in depth research (it’s LLVM’s fault) here11 posts - 6 participants
